description:
No. 125 was the highest number on the Soviet Georgian green tea scale. The scale began at No. 10, the lowest quality, and the number rose with the grade; only Bouquet and Extra sat above 125.

The number is a grade rather than a recipe. It tells you where the tea ranked, and very little is recorded about how this lot differed in the making from those around it.

Taste notes for it are missing, so expect only what is usual for a leaf green. Water around 80 °C and a moderate steep is the safe start.

If you meet the number today, ask who made the tea. It may be a nostalgic label rather than the old standard.
history:
The numbered system comes from the Soviet period, when Georgia produced a wide range of green grades. No. 125 marked the best of the top numbered grade, and Georgian accounts also list it among the teas of the highest class.

Little is documented about who set the grade or when it stopped being made.
